premises: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi HEAs contain a high density of microstructural defects (dislocations, internal strains, grain boundaries).
These defects create a broad distribution of local exchange interactions.
This broad distribution governs the sharp, hysteretic magnetostructural transition.
Mild annealing reduces defect density and homogenizes exchange interactions.
Homogenized exchange interactions broaden the magnetocaloric peak and reduce hysteresis.
